s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly growing, variegated skin lesion with recent color change
salient_findings: Enlarged and variegated plaque on the left axilla
Lesion has well-demarcated margins and a dark brown color
Intraepidermal neoplasm with pagetoid cells on histopathology
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 70s
The lesion has been present for 4 years
The lesion started as a small eczematous, pink-to-brown plaque
The lesion is asymptomatic
The lesion has recently changed to a dark brown color
No breast mass or lymphadenopathy is observed
Incisional biopsy revealed an intraepidermal neoplasm
Pagetoid cells have round, pale vacuolated cytoplasm and large pleomorphic nuclei
Immunohistochemical staining is positive for CK7 and EMA
Numerous reactive dendritic HMB-45–positive melanocytes are scattered among tumor cells

shortlist.label: Extramammary Paget's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Pagetoid cells with positive CK7 and EMA staining

shortlist.label: Pagetoid Bowen's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Intraepidermal neoplasm with pagetoid cells and recent color change

shortlist.label: Malignant melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Recent change to dark brown color and presence of melanocytes

shortlist.label: Apocrine gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Positive staining for CK7 and presence of pagetoid cells

shortlist.label: Intraepidermal adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Intraepidermal neoplasm with positive EMA staining

raw.rationale: The presence of an intraepidermal neoplasm with pagetoid cells, positive staining for CK7 and EMA, and the location of the lesion in the axilla are consistent with Extramammary Paget's disease

rejected.label: Pagetoid Bowen's disease
rejected.why: Lack of typical Bowen's disease histological features

rejected.label: Malignant melanoma
rejected.why: Immunohistochemical staining pattern does not support melanoma

rejected.label: Apocrine gland carcinoma
rejected.why: Histopathology does not indicate apocrine gland involvement
